newsitem.title: USA: Checkers financing in flux after Q3 loss.
newsitem.headline: Checkers financing in flux after Q3 loss.

text.p: Checkers Drive-In Restaurants Inc said its third-quarter results, which sustained a much wider net loss from the year-ago period, has caused it to be unable to meet the conditions of its latest financial convenants.

Checkers announced on September 17 that it reached an agreement in principle on debt restructuring with a group of capital management funds. In an announcement released Friday, the company said it was now unable to meet the conditions of that agreeement "due in large part to the charges and loss provisions taken in the third quarter."

In the statement, the company said its net loss for the third was $0.47 per share, compared with a loss of $0.14 per share in the third quarter of 1995. Its loss for the nine months of 1996 totals $0.50 per share, compared with a loss of $0.20 per share for the nine months of 1995.

The results contained in Friday's release conflict with the third-quarter results released on October 18. Those results show a third-quarter loss of $0.46 per share and a nine-month loss of $0.49 per share.
The company was not immediately available to comment on the discrepancy.

Checkers said its efforts to further restructure the debt financing with its financing group has been unsuccessful. The financing group told Checkers it considering selling Checkers' debt package to a third party.
Checkers said it believes the financing group has delayed further restructuring while it tries to find a buyer.

The financing group has extended the loan default waivers until November 8, Checkers said. The company said it would continue to try to restructure its current debt package with the financing group or with whoever may buy or assume the debt package, and said it will also seek further outside third-party financing.
Checkers said it "does not currently have the ability to cure the payment defaults or financial convenant defaults that have occured or been waived to date."
"We are working very closely with the investor group to address all of these issues," Albert DiMarco, Checkers' chief executive, said in a statement accompanying the announcement.
